tasks.prompt: Graduate-path practice: imagine you are a teaching assistant invited to lead one 75-minute session of an introductory American politics course on 'Why turnout differs across groups and elections'. Design the session: learning goals, two short readings you would assign (real, cited), a mini-lecture outline, an activity using public turnout data, discussion questions that require evidence, and a short assessment. Explain how you would keep the session nonpartisan.

rubric.description: Covers recognized explanations of turnout (costs of voting, mobilization, resources, election type, institutional rules) accurately.
Includes a data activity and evidence-based discussion questions.
Has an assessment aligned to the goals and a clear approach to nonpartisan teaching.

reference_answer_outline: Goals: explain three drivers of turnout and interpret turnout data.
Readings: a classic article on the calculus of voting and a recent study on registration rules, cited.
Activity: compare midterm and presidential turnout by age using census voting supplement tables.
Discussion: which reforms would most change the gaps, and what evidence supports that?
Assessment: one-paragraph data interpretation; neutrality by focusing on evidence and multiple perspectives.

tasks.task_intent: Adjust teaching approaches and materials to suit students' different needs and interests.
tasks.prompt: Your 9th-grade civics class of 30 includes four English learners at intermediate proficiency, two students with reading-related learning disabilities, and several students who already follow politics closely. Take a lesson on the First Amendment's freedoms and adapt it: the common learning goal, three versions of the main reading or source set, a choice-based task with different entry points, supports and extensions, grouping strategies, and how you assess everyone against the same goal.

rubric.description: All students work toward the same core goal with differentiated materials and processes.
Supports for English learners and students with disabilities are concrete (glossaries, audio, sentence frames, chunked texts).
Assessment measures the same goal for all students, with accommodations that do not lower expectations.

reference_answer_outline: Goal: explain how a First Amendment freedom applies in a realistic scenario.
Materials: adapted text, original text with annotations, audio version; images and case summaries.
Task choice: case brief, short podcast script, or annotated poster on a student-speech case.
Groups mixed by skill with roles; extension using an actual court opinion excerpt.
Rubric shared by all products, focused on applying the freedom correctly.

tasks.task_intent: Check that data entered into research databases are accurate and valid, and fix the errors found.
tasks.prompt: A project codes local news articles into a protest-event dataset (date, location, issue, size estimate, police presence). Four coders have entered 1,200 events. Design the verification procedure: a double-coding sample, which variables you compute intercoder reliability for and with which statistic, logic and range checks (dates outside the study period, size estimates as text), how disagreements are resolved and recorded, and the reliability threshold below which a variable's coding rules must be revised.

rubric.description: Uses an appropriate statistic (such as Krippendorff's alpha or Cohen's kappa) on a sufficient random sample, per variable.
Specifies automated validity checks and manual review of flagged records.
Disagreements are resolved by rule with an audit trail, and low-reliability variables trigger codebook revision and recoding.

reference_answer_outline: Random 15 percent of articles double-coded blind.
Alpha per variable; categorical issue codes and size bins.
Checks: dates in range, valid place names geocoded, numeric size fields.
Adjudication by a lead coder; log of original codes and final decisions.
Threshold around 0.8 for key variables, 0.67 minimum for tentative use; revise rules and retrain otherwise.

tasks.task_intent: Find the questions that are worth researching and analyzing.
tasks.prompt: Graduate-path practice: a county elections office asks a local university for help understanding why turnout in municipal elections is below 20 percent. Write a research agenda memo: three candidate research questions ranked by importance and feasibility, what is already known (cite at least two real studies), the data that exist or could be collected, which question you would pursue first and why, and ethical or political sensitivities in working with an elections office.

rubric.description: Questions are specific, answerable and policy-relevant (e.g. effect of election timing or mail ballots).
Cites real prior work and identifies feasible data sources.
Justifies the choice with explicit criteria and addresses neutrality, privacy of voter files and independence.

reference_answer_outline: Questions: does moving local elections to coincide with state elections raise turnout; do mailed reminders work; who are habitual non-voters?
Literature on election timing and turnout, and on low-cost mobilization field experiments.
Data: voter files with turnout history, election calendars, mail ballot records.
Pursue first: a feasible randomized reminder study with the office.
Ethics: protect voter data, nonpartisan messages, pre-registration of the study.

tasks.task_intent: Produce sophisticated motion graphics on the computer, relying on one's own creative judgment.
tasks.prompt: A city transit agency wants a 20-second silent animated explainer, for station screens, showing how to tap a contactless card or phone to pay. Write the production plan and creative rationale: a short storyboard (six to eight frames with timing), the visual style and color palette tied to the agency's brand and accessibility, how motion guides attention without text, the software and file formats you will use, and how you will test that riders understand it without sound.

rubric.description: Storyboard communicates the steps in sequence with timing that fits 20 seconds.
Style, contrast and motion choices support comprehension, including for viewers with low vision or limited English.
Names tools and output specs and includes a comprehension test with riders.

reference_answer_outline: Frames: approach gate, hold card near reader, light or check mark feedback, gate opens, phone variant.
Brand palette with high contrast; large icons; no essential text.
Motion: highlight reader with gentle pulse; ease-in timing; loop cleanly.
Tools: vector design and motion graphics software; export at screen resolution and frame rate.
Test with ten riders: can they describe the steps after one viewing?

tasks.task_intent: Decide how big images and text should be, how they are arranged on the page, and which typefaces and sizes to use.
tasks.prompt: Design a poster (24 by 36 inches) for a free community jazz festival with a headline, date and location, five performer names, a sponsor logo strip and a QR code. Write the layout and typography specification: grid and margins, the visual hierarchy (what is read first, second, third), typeface choices and sizes in points with reasons, image placement and scale, color and contrast, and how the design adapts to a 1080 by 1920 pixel social media version.

rubric.description: Arrangement makes the most important information readable first from a distance.
Typefaces, sizes and spacing are specified and justified for legibility and mood.
Explains how the layout adapts to a vertical digital format without losing hierarchy.

reference_answer_outline: Grid: 12 columns, margins about 1 inch, generous whitespace.
Hierarchy: festival name, then date and place, then performers, then sponsors and QR code.
Type: display face for the headline at large size; clean sans serif for details; at most two families.
Image: full-bleed illustration with text on a calm area; contrast checked.
Social version: stacked layout, larger date, QR code replaced by link.

tasks.task_intent: Work with front-end and back-end developers so a website project is delivered completely.
tasks.prompt: You designed an online exhibit for a local history museum with scroll-triggered animations, an interactive timeline and an image zoom viewer, to be built by one front-end and one back-end developer. Write the collaboration plan: how you specify animations (timing, easing, reduced-motion alternatives), the content model the back end must support (timeline entries, image sets, captions, credits), performance budgets for images and scripts, how you pair with developers during build, and acceptance testing.

rubric.description: Animation and interaction specs are concrete enough to build and include accessibility alternatives.
Defines a content model and performance budgets that developers can implement.
Describes pairing, feedback loops and acceptance tests.

reference_answer_outline: Motion specs with durations and easing; prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
Content model fields: date, title, text, images, alt text, credits.
Budgets: page weight limit, responsive images, lazy loading.
Weekly pairing sessions and a shared issues board.
Acceptance: device matrix, keyboard navigation, screen reader check, performance score.

tasks.task_intent: Make digital objects and characters look believable through careful handling of lighting, surface color and texture, shadows and see-through materials, or by bringing still images to life.
tasks.prompt: A kitchenware company needs a photorealistic 3D render of a glass-and-steel kettle for its website, matching studio product photography. Write the lighting, materials and rendering plan: the light setup (key, fill, rim, environment map), physically based material settings for brushed steel, clear glass with water inside and a rubber handle, how you handle reflections, caustics and shadows, the render settings, and how you compare the result with reference photos.

rubric.description: Light setup is purposeful and mimics studio product photography.
Material parameters (roughness, index of refraction, anisotropy) are appropriate for each material.
Describes how renders are evaluated against real photos and adjusted.

reference_answer_outline: Large soft key, fill card, rim light for edges, neutral HDRI for reflections.
Steel: metallic with anisotropic roughness; glass: refractive index around 1.5; water slightly higher.
Shadows: soft contact shadow; caustics enabled or faked for speed.
Render samples and denoising settings; output color space.
Side-by-side with reference shots; adjust highlights and reflections.

tasks.task_intent: Draw early sketches or illustrations, talk them through with the client or art lead, and rework them.
tasks.prompt: A neighborhood bakery wants a new logo and storefront sign. Describe your concept phase: how you gather the brief (values, audience, competitors), six thumbnail directions in words, how you narrow to three rough sketches, how you present them to the owners and capture feedback, and how you revise without losing the concept. Include the questions you ask when feedback is vague (such as 'make it pop').

rubric.description: Concepts clearly connect to the brief and are distinct.
Presentation explains rationale and gathers specific, usable feedback.
Revisions respond to feedback while protecting legibility and concept, with documented approvals.

reference_answer_outline: Brief questionnaire and a mood board.
Thumbnails: hand-lettered script, wheat icon, vintage badge, minimalist wordmark, illustrative storefront, geometric bread shape.
Three roughs shown on a mockup sign at real scale.
Clarifying questions: which part should stand out, what feeling is missing, show an example you like.
Revision round with change log and owner sign-off.

tasks.task_intent: Lead pre-production work such as mood boards, storyboards and the project timeline.
tasks.prompt: A food-rescue nonprofit hires you to redesign its website to recruit volunteers and donors. Write the pre-production plan: discovery activities, two mood boards described in words with the reasoning behind each, a storyboard of the volunteer sign-up journey from home page to confirmation, content and asset inventory, roles and approvals, and a six-week timeline with milestones and review points.

rubric.description: Discovery identifies users, goals and constraints before visual work.
Mood boards and storyboard are specific and tied to goals.
Timeline has milestones, review points and dependencies on client content.

reference_answer_outline: Discovery: stakeholder interview, analytics review, three volunteer interviews.
Mood board A: warm, community photography; B: bold, data-driven impact graphics.
Storyboard: home, volunteer page, choose shift, form, confirmation email.
Inventory: photos, impact numbers, copy, logos.
Weeks 1 to 6 with approvals after mood boards and wireframes.

tasks.task_intent: Check prescriptions for correctness, work out what is needed to fill them, and judge whether they are appropriate for the patient.
tasks.prompt: Invented case for practice under pharmacist supervision: a prescription arrives for an 82-year-old woman (weight 52 kg, recent serum creatinine 1.6 mg/dL) for an antibiotic at the full adult dose usually used with normal kidney function, plus a new prescription for an NSAID; her profile shows an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic. Write the verification you would perform: the checks for completeness and legality, estimating kidney function (show a Cockcroft-Gault calculation), dose appropriateness, the interaction concern, what you would recommend to the prescriber, and how you document the intervention.

rubric.description: Checks patient identifiers, prescriber details, drug, dose, route, frequency, quantity and legality before clinical review.
Calculates creatinine clearance correctly, recognizes the need for renal dose adjustment and the NSAID plus ACE inhibitor plus diuretic kidney risk.
Recommends specific alternatives to the prescriber and documents the call and outcome.

reference_answer_outline: Completeness: patient name, date of birth, drug strength, directions, prescriber signature and identifiers.
Cockcroft-Gault: (140 minus age) times weight divided by (72 times creatinine), times 0.85 for women; about 25 mL/min.
Check the antibiotic's labeled renal dosing and suggest an adjusted dose or interval.
NSAID with ACE inhibitor and diuretic raises acute kidney injury risk; suggest acetaminophen or topical alternative.
Document recommendation, prescriber response and final action in the profile.

tasks.task_intent: Advise patients about how a drug interacts with others, its side effects, how much to take and how to store it.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a 67-year-old man is starting an oral anticoagulant after a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation; he takes an over-the-counter pain reliever several times a week, uses a fish-oil supplement and sometimes forgets evening doses of other medicines. Write the counseling script: opening and teach-back, how to take the medicine and what to do about a missed dose (per the product labeling), bleeding warning signs, interactions with his OTC products, storage, and when to call the pharmacist or doctor or seek emergency care.

rubric.description: Advice reflects the drug's labeling and addresses his OTC pain reliever and supplement use.
Clearly explains bleeding signs and emergency situations.
Uses plain language, teach-back and adherence aids for forgetfulness.

reference_answer_outline: Open with purpose and ask what he already knows.
Dosing and missed-dose instructions from the labeling; pill organizer or phone alarm.
Bleeding signs: black stools, blood in urine, unusual bruising, severe headache; seek urgent care for serious signs.
Avoid routine NSAID use; discuss fish oil with the prescriber; acetaminophen as a usual alternative within limits.
Teach-back: he explains how and when he takes it and what he watches for.

tasks.task_intent: Keep pharmacy records such as patient profiles, inventories and controlled-drug logs.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: during the monthly count of a Schedule II opioid at a community pharmacy, the physical count is 40 tablets short of the perpetual inventory. Write the reconciliation and records procedure: how you recount and review dispensing records, receiving invoices and transfer documents, common clerical causes to check, when a loss must be reported to the regulator and the board of pharmacy (refer to the applicable rules without inventing numbers), how you secure records, and what process changes you would make.

rubric.description: Reviews every relevant record type and checks for clerical errors before concluding loss.
States that significant losses or thefts must be reported to the appropriate authorities on the required form and timeline.
Proposes concrete controls such as more frequent counts, access restrictions and camera review.

reference_answer_outline: Recount with a second person; compare with perpetual log.
Review prescriptions filled, partial fills, returns to stock, invoices, transfer forms.
Clerical checks: wrong package size entered, unposted returns.
If unresolved, report theft or significant loss per federal and state rules.
Controls: daily counts for high-risk items, restricted safe access, audit trail.

tasks.task_intent: Help customers choose among medicine brands, medical equipment and health supplies.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a parent asks for help choosing a cough and cold product for a 4-year-old, and her own father wants a home blood-pressure monitor. Write both consultations: the questions you ask first, the reasons you would not recommend certain products for young children, safe options for the child, how you explain dosing by weight and measuring devices, criteria for choosing a validated, correctly sized blood-pressure cuff, and when you refer to a physician.

rubric.description: Asks about symptoms, age, weight, other conditions and medicines before recommending.
Avoids inappropriate OTC cough and cold products for young children and suggests safe measures; dosing guidance is accurate.
Explains validated monitors, cuff sizing and technique, and gives clear referral criteria.

reference_answer_outline: Questions: fever, breathing difficulty, duration, chronic conditions, other medicines.
Many cough and cold combinations are not advised for young children; suggest saline, fluids, humidified air, honey only for children over one year.
Weight-based acetaminophen or ibuprofen if fever, with the correct measuring device.
Monitor: upper-arm, validated, cuff fitted to arm circumference; measurement technique.
Refer for breathing problems, high fever, symptoms beyond about 10 days, or very high readings.

tasks.task_intent: Plan, carry out or maintain procedures for compounding, packaging or labeling medicines according to policy and law, covering quality, security and disposal.
tasks.prompt: Your community pharmacy will start preparing a non-sterile oral suspension for children from tablets. Write the standard operating procedure: master formulation record and compounding record contents, beyond-use dating source, equipment and cleaning, ingredient verification and calculations double-checked, labeling contents, storage and security, quality checks before release, and how waste and expired compounds are disposed of. Reference the type of standard (such as the national compendial chapter for non-sterile compounding) rather than inventing specific requirements.

rubric.description: Procedure follows recognized non-sterile compounding standards and pharmacy law.
Includes independent verification of calculations, ingredients and final product.
Specifies label contents, storage conditions, beyond-use date and proper disposal of waste.

reference_answer_outline: Master formulation record with ingredients, quantities, method, beyond-use date source.
Compounding record: lot numbers, operator, checker, date.
Calibrated balance, clean area and equipment cleaning log.
Label: name, strength, directions, beyond-use date, 'shake well', storage.
Disposal of waste and expired product per environmental and pharmacy rules.

tasks.task_intent: Look for patterns in prescriptions to track whether patients take medicines as directed and to prevent overuse or dangerous combinations.
tasks.prompt: Invented data: in your pharmacy's records for the last six months, 38 patients filled both an opioid and a benzodiazepine, 12 of them from different prescribers, and adherence to statins among 400 patients averaged a proportion of days covered of 0.68. Write the analysis and action plan: how you compute and interpret proportion of days covered, how you identify high-risk combinations and early refills (including use of the state prescription monitoring program), which patients you prioritize, and the interventions with prescribers and patients, while respecting privacy.

rubric.description: Explains proportion of days covered and adherence thresholds correctly.
Identifies high-risk opioid plus benzodiazepine use, multiple prescribers and early refills using appropriate tools.
Plans prioritized, respectful interventions such as prescriber outreach, naloxone offers and adherence counseling.

reference_answer_outline: PDC: days covered divided by days in period; common adherence threshold near 0.80.
Flag patients with overlapping opioid and benzodiazepine fills and multiple prescribers; check monitoring program.
Prioritize high doses, multiple prescribers, recent overdose history.
Interventions: prescriber calls, naloxone, counseling; adherence packaging and refill synchronization for statins.
Use minimum necessary data; document interventions.

tasks.task_intent: Keep patient records and reports that are accurate, complete and detailed.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: on a medical-surgical unit, Mr. R., 72, two days after bowel surgery, became confused at 02:00, pulled at his IV, had a temperature of 38.4 C and a heart rate of 112. You notified the on-call provider, a blood culture was drawn and his daughter was called. Write (1) the narrative or focused nursing note for these events and (2) the SBAR handoff you would give the day nurse at 07:00. Then list three charting errors a reviewer commonly finds in notes like this and how your note avoids them.

rubric.description: The note is factual, timed, and objective (observed behaviors and measured values, not labels like 'difficult'), and includes interventions and the patient's response.
SBAR covers situation, relevant background, current assessment and a clear recommendation or pending items such as culture results.
Identifies real charting pitfalls (late entries without labeling, vague times, copying forward, unapproved abbreviations) and shows how the note avoids them.

reference_answer_outline: Timed entries: assessment findings, provider notification time and orders received, actions taken, reassessment.
Describes confusion with orientation findings and safety measures (bed alarm, IV secured) rather than judgments.
SBAR: new-onset confusion with fever and tachycardia; post-op day 2; current vitals and mental status; recommend follow-up on cultures and reassessment.
Pitfalls: missing times, unexplained abbreviations, charting care before it is done; corrections made per policy.
Family notification documented with who was called and what was said.

tasks.task_intent: Weigh the reasons for and against a treatment, its possible complications, and its costs against its benefits.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: Mrs. T., 81, is on day 3 after hip-fracture repair and still has an indwelling urinary catheter placed in surgery. The night nurse wants to keep it because she is slow to walk to the bathroom. Write a one-page analysis comparing keeping the catheter with removing it today: clinical indications and contraindications for each option, risks (including infection, retention, falls, skin breakdown), cost considerations, what you would assess before deciding, and the recommendation you would bring to the provider. Cite the type of evidence (e.g. hospital protocol, nursing guidelines) you would check.

rubric.description: Correctly distinguishes valid catheter indications (such as retention or strict output monitoring) from convenience, and applies them to the case.
Compares infection and retention risk with fall and mobility risk, and notes cost of a hospital-acquired infection versus nursing time.
Recommends a clear action with a monitoring plan (bladder scan, voiding trial, toileting schedule) and when to escalate.

reference_answer_outline: Convenience is not an indication; check for retention, strict output needs or sacral wounds.
Keeping it raises catheter-associated urinary tract infection risk with each day; removal risks retention and falls if toileting support is poor.
Assess voiding history, bladder scan capability, mobility and cognition, pain control.
Recommend removal with a voiding trial, scheduled toileting, fall precautions and bladder scanning per protocol.
Check the unit's catheter-removal protocol and current nursing guidance on catheter-associated infection prevention.

tasks.task_intent: Care for a patient's body after death in a respectful way.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a patient in the ICU has died after the family chose comfort care. The family is on the way, the patient is Muslim, and the attending mentioned the case may need medical examiner review because of a recent fall. Write the after-death care procedure you would follow: what you check before touching lines and tubes, how you prepare the body and room for the family, how you respect religious and cultural wishes, the notifications required (including organ and tissue donation referral), and what you document.

rubric.description: Confirms pronouncement and whether a medical examiner case requires leaving lines and tubes in place before removing anything.
Prepares the body and room respectfully, asks the family about religious practices (such as same-sex handling or washing), and offers time and support.
Includes required notifications (provider, donation organization per hospital policy, chaplain if wanted) and documents times, belongings and who was present.

reference_answer_outline: Verify time of death documentation; ask whether the case is reportable before removing devices.
If not reportable, remove or cap devices per policy; position the body, close eyes, clean gently, fresh linen, dim lights.
Ask the family about rituals; offer a chaplain or imam; respect requests regarding who handles the body.
Notify the organ procurement organization within the required time per policy.
Document belongings, notifications, family presence and transfer to the morgue or funeral home.

tasks.task_intent: Watch for symptoms or changes in a patient's condition, record them and report them.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: you are caring for five patients on a step-down unit. One, a 58-year-old with pneumonia, had a respiratory rate of 18 and oxygen saturation of 95 percent on 2 L at 08:00; at 11:00 the rate is 26, saturation 90 percent and she says she feels 'off'. Write (1) a monitoring plan for this patient for the rest of the shift, (2) how you calculate an early-warning score or apply your unit's rapid-response criteria, (3) the exact SBAR call to the provider, and (4) what you record and when.

rubric.description: Identifies the trend as deterioration, considers other vital signs and mental status, and reassesses promptly rather than waiting for the next scheduled check.
Applies early-warning or rapid-response criteria correctly and gives a concise SBAR with a specific request.
Records values, times, interventions and responses, and states the reassessment interval.

reference_answer_outline: Immediate reassessment: full vitals, work of breathing, lung sounds, mental status, oxygen delivery check.
Calculate an early-warning score from respiratory rate, saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature and consciousness; trigger the rapid-response team if the threshold is met.
SBAR: rising respiratory rate and falling saturation over three hours; request bedside evaluation and orders such as blood gas or chest imaging.
Interventions within scope: raise head of bed, titrate oxygen per protocol.
Document each value with time, notification time, response and recheck every 15 to 30 minutes until stable.

tasks.task_intent: Manage pain and sedation with both drug and non-drug measures, watch how the patient responds, and change the plan as needed.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: Mr. L., 45, is one day after open abdominal surgery, using a patient-controlled analgesia pump with an opioid. He rates pain 8/10 when coughing, 4/10 at rest, and has snoring episodes with brief pauses in breathing; he has a history of sleep apnea and his CPAP machine is at home. Write a nursing care plan: assessment tools you will use (pain and sedation scales), non-drug measures, what you would ask the provider about multimodal analgesia, the monitoring needed for respiratory depression, and the criteria that would make you change or escalate the plan.

rubric.description: Uses a validated pain scale and a sedation scale (such as POSS or RASS) and assesses function, not only pain numbers.
Recognizes sleep apnea plus opioids as high risk and plans continuous monitoring (pulse oximetry, capnography if available) and getting CPAP.
Includes non-drug measures, multimodal options to discuss, and explicit criteria for holding doses or escalating.

reference_answer_outline: Pain at rest and with activity; sedation score before and after doses.
Non-drug measures: splinting pillow for coughing, positioning, early walking, cold or heat as allowed.
Ask about scheduled non-opioid analgesics or regional techniques to reduce opioid need.
Continuous oxygen saturation and, if available, end-tidal CO2 monitoring; arrange for his CPAP or a hospital device.
Hold or reduce opioid and notify the provider if sedation rises or respiratory rate falls below protocol limits; naloxone available.

tasks.task_intent: Partner with the wider care team to build and update the plan of care, grounded in the patient's needs and assessment findings.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: an ICU patient, 67, is on day 6 of mechanical ventilation for pneumonia, is now more alert, has not had a bowel movement in four days, and has a stage 2 pressure injury on the sacrum. Prepare what you will bring to tomorrow's interdisciplinary rounds: a two-minute nursing summary, the specific questions or proposals for the physician, respiratory therapist, pharmacist, dietitian and physical therapist, and how you will record agreed changes to the plan of care and follow up on them.

rubric.description: The summary prioritizes the issues most relevant to the plan (readiness to wean, mobility, skin, bowels) with current assessment data.
Each team member gets a concrete question or proposal within their expertise (spontaneous breathing trial, bowel regimen review, nutrition for wound healing, early mobility).
Changes are documented in the care plan with owners and times, and the nurse checks they happen.

reference_answer_outline: Summary: vent settings and trend, sedation level, skin and bowel status, family update.
Respiratory therapist and physician: is the patient ready for a sedation pause and spontaneous breathing trial?
Pharmacist: review opioid and sedative doses and add a bowel regimen; dietitian: protein and calories for wound healing.
Physical therapist: progressive mobility plan; nursing: repositioning schedule and support surface.
Record agreed actions with owners; check at end of shift and report to the next nurse.

tasks.task_intent: Give project team members their duties and responsibilities.
tasks.prompt: You are the project specialist for moving a 60-person insurance office to a new building in eight weeks. The team: facilities coordinator, IT technician, HR generalist, an office manager, two volunteer 'floor captains', and the moving vendor. Build a responsibility assignment (RACI) matrix for the twelve main work packages, explain how you matched duties to people's skills and workloads, how you will confirm each person accepts their assignments, and how you will rebalance if someone becomes overloaded.

rubric.description: Each work package has exactly one accountable owner, and responsible, consulted and informed roles are sensible.
Assignments reflect skills, authority and availability rather than convenience.
Includes a step for confirming assignments and a concrete method for detecting and fixing overload.

reference_answer_outline: Work packages: floor plan, IT network and phones, furniture, vendor contract, employee communication, packing, security badges, parking, mail forwarding, go-live support.
IT technician accountable for network cutover; HR for employee communication; facilities for vendor coordination.
Kickoff meeting where owners confirm scope and capacity.
Weekly status check of hours and task counts per person.
Rebalance by shifting tasks to floor captains or adding vendor support.

tasks.task_intent: Collect information about a business problem or process and organize it so it can be analyzed.
tasks.prompt: A regional hospital's outpatient clinic says patients wait too long for appointments and staff blame 'the scheduling system'. You are the management analyst assigned to find out what is really happening. Write the information-gathering plan: who you will interview and what you will ask, what data you will pull (scheduling records, no-show rates, provider templates), what you will observe in person, and how you will organize the findings (process map, issue log, data summary) so they can be analyzed next week.

rubric.description: Combines interviews, system data and direct observation and includes front-line staff and patients, not only managers.
Questions and data requests target the problem (lead time to appointment, template rules, no-shows, cancellations).
Specifies the structure for organizing information so it can be analyzed and verified.

reference_answer_outline: Interviews: schedulers, nurses, two providers, clinic manager, a handful of patients.
Data: days to third-next-available appointment, no-show and late cancel rates, template blocks by provider, call abandonment.
Observation: shadow the scheduling desk for a morning.
Organize: current-state process map, issue log tagged by cause, summary tables.
Validate findings with a short readback session with staff.

tasks.task_intent: Plan and carry out recruiting approaches that meet current and expected staffing needs.
tasks.prompt: A growing regional logistics company must hire 40 warehouse associates and 6 shift supervisors in the next four months for a new distribution center, in a town with low unemployment. Write the recruiting strategy: the workforce need by role and month, target candidate sources, the employer value proposition you would promote, the selection process with time-to-hire targets, how you ensure fair and lawful hiring, and the metrics you will track weekly.

rubric.description: Ties sourcing volume to the hiring target using realistic funnel assumptions (applicants per hire).
Sources and messaging fit a tight local market (referral bonuses, community partners, shift flexibility, internal promotion for supervisors).
Includes consistent structured selection and lawful practices, plus weekly metrics such as time-to-fill and offer acceptance.

reference_answer_outline: Hiring calendar: ramp by month to match the facility opening.
Funnel: estimated applicants per hire for associates and supervisors.
Sources: job boards, workforce centers, community colleges, referral bonus, internal postings for supervisors.
Structured interviews with scored questions; consistent background-check policy.
Metrics: applicants, interviews, offers, acceptances, 90-day retention.

tasks.task_intent: Work with key stakeholders to pin down what a project must deliver and why.
tasks.prompt: A city library system wants a project to add self-service laptop lending kiosks at four branches. Stakeholders include branch managers, IT, the finance office, the library board, and patrons. Plan a two-hour requirements workshop and its outputs: the agenda, techniques you will use to draw out needs and conflicts, how you will separate objectives from solutions, a draft project charter section listing objectives with success measures, and how disagreements will be resolved.

rubric.description: Agenda and techniques give all stakeholder groups a voice, including patron input gathered beforehand.
Objectives are specific and measurable (e.g. availability rate, cost per loan, damage rate), separate from solution features.
States a clear decision process for conflicting requirements, such as a priority scheme and a sponsor decision.

reference_answer_outline: Pre-work: short patron survey and branch usage data.
Agenda: purpose, current-state stories, needs brainstorming, prioritization, constraints, next steps.
Techniques: affinity grouping, MoSCoW prioritization, dot voting.
Charter: objectives with targets, scope, constraints (budget, privacy), assumptions.
Escalate unresolved conflicts to the project sponsor with options documented.

tasks.task_intent: Make sense of the information collected and propose fixes or other ways forward.
tasks.prompt: Invented findings from the clinic study: average wait to a new appointment is 34 days; 18 percent of booked slots are no-shows; providers each block 4 hours a week that are often unused; schedulers spend 30 percent of their time on reminder calls; and appointment types have 11 different lengths. Write the analysis and options paper: root causes supported by the data, three alternative solutions (for example, automated reminders, template simplification, overbooking rules or open-access scheduling), the expected impact and cost of each, risks, and the recommended sequence.

rubric.description: Root causes are linked to the evidence and quantified where possible (lost capacity from no-shows and unused blocks).
Options are distinct, with impact estimates, costs and risks.
Recommends a sequence with quick wins and a pilot, and how success will be measured.

reference_answer_outline: Lost capacity estimate from no-shows and unused blocked time.
Option 1: automated text reminders to cut no-shows and free scheduler time.
Option 2: simplify appointment lengths to three or four types.
Option 3: release unused blocked time 48 hours ahead; limited overbooking based on no-show prediction.
Pilot in one clinic for eight weeks, measure wait time and no-show rate.

tasks.task_intent: Make HR rules, workplace laws and company procedures understandable to employees and managers.
tasks.prompt: A 200-employee company is introducing a new paid leave policy because of a new state paid sick leave law, and managers are confused about how it interacts with existing vacation days and with federal family and medical leave. Write a one-page manager brief and a ten-question employee FAQ: what the policy provides, accrual and use rules, documentation that can and cannot be requested, non-retaliation, and where to get help. Note which points you would confirm with legal counsel, and invent no specific statutory numbers without labeling them as placeholders.

rubric.description: Explains rules clearly, labels placeholders for state-specific figures, and flags items needing legal confirmation.
The manager brief focuses on what managers must do; the FAQ uses plain language employees can act on.
Covers non-retaliation, confidentiality of medical information and consistent application.

reference_answer_outline: Brief: what changes, effective date, manager duties (approve, record, never discourage use).
Accrual rate placeholder, carryover and caps, permitted uses including family care.
Documentation: limits on asking for medical details; follow the law's thresholds.
Interaction with vacation and family and medical leave explained with an example.
FAQ ends with HR contact and a confidential reporting channel.

tasks.task_intent: Review a department's monthly budget and accounting reports to keep spending under control.
tasks.prompt: Invented data: a county parks department's year-to-date report at the end of month 7 (of 12) shows: personnel 4.1 of 7.2 million budgeted, seasonal staff 0.62 of 0.80 million, utilities 0.55 of 0.84 million, equipment repair 0.31 of 0.36 million, and program revenue 0.95 of 2.0 million expected. Write a variance analysis memo for the parks director: compute expected spending at this point (straight-line and, where it applies, seasonal), identify which lines are on track or at risk, explain likely causes and questions to ask, project year-end results, and recommend controls.

rubric.description: Calculates percentage used versus elapsed time correctly and adjusts for seasonality where it obviously applies (seasonal staff, summer program revenue).
Separates timing differences from real overruns and names plausible causes and follow-up questions.
Recommends specific controls (hiring freeze on certain lines, purchase approvals, revenue review) and a year-end projection.

reference_answer_outline: Elapsed time about 58 percent; personnel at 57 percent is on track.
Seasonal staff at 78 percent may be normal after summer but must be checked against the season calendar.
Equipment repair at 86 percent is a real overrun risk; ask about aging mowers or one-time repairs.
Program revenue at 48 percent with peak season over suggests a shortfall; project year-end.
Controls: pre-approval for repairs above a threshold, monthly revenue review, possible mid-year budget amendment.

tasks.task_intent: Write thorough reports on what an audit found.
tasks.prompt: Invented engagement: an internal audit of a university's purchasing cards (500 cardholders) tested 60 transactions and found 7 without receipts, 3 split purchases that avoided the bid threshold, 2 personal purchases later repaid, and approvers who signed off on their own statements in one department. Write the audit findings report: an executive summary, each finding written as condition, criteria, cause, effect and recommendation, a risk rating for each, management's response section (with placeholders), and the follow-up timeline.

rubric.description: Each finding states condition, criteria (the policy breached), cause, effect and recommendation clearly.
Ratings reflect severity and pervasiveness; self-approval and split purchases are treated as control failures, not paperwork issues.
Factual, non-accusatory language, room for management responses, and dates for follow-up testing.

reference_answer_outline: Executive summary with overall conclusion and the top two risks.
Missing receipts: 7 of 60 (about 12 percent) against the receipt policy; cause and recommendation.
Split purchases avoiding bid rules: high risk; recommend analytics to detect splitting.
Self-approval: segregation-of-duties failure; recommend system-enforced approver hierarchy.
Personal use repaid: policy violation; recommend training and card suspension rules; follow-up in six months.

tasks.task_intent: Put together loan applications, including the credit analysis and a summary of the request, and forward them for the loan committee's decision.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a family-owned bakery with three years of tax returns (revenue 820k, 910k, 1.04 million; net income 41k, 55k, 72k), existing debt payments of 3,000 per month, and a request for 180,000 over seven years to buy a second oven line. Write the credit memo you would submit to the loan committee: the request summary, analysis of profitability, cash flow and debt service coverage (show the calculation), collateral and guarantees, key risks and mitigants, and your recommendation with any conditions.

rubric.description: Calculates a debt service coverage ratio from cash available for debt service and new plus existing payments, with assumptions stated.
Identifies business-specific risks (owner dependence, ingredient costs, single location) and mitigants.
Clear recommendation with conditions, such as covenants or a personal guarantee, consistent with the analysis.

reference_answer_outline: Summary: borrower, purpose, amount, term, rate assumption, repayment source.
Trend: revenue up about 27 percent over two years; margins improving.
Debt service: estimate the new monthly payment; coverage equals cash flow (net income plus depreciation and interest) over total annual debt payments; compare with a typical minimum near 1.25.
Collateral: equipment lien; personal guarantee from owners.
Recommend approval with a coverage covenant and annual financial statements if coverage is adequate.

tasks.task_intent: Lead the preparation of routine and special-purpose budget reports.
tasks.prompt: You are the budget analyst who must deliver two products for a mid-size nonprofit: the regular quarterly budget-to-actual report for the board finance committee, and a special report on the cost of opening a new after-school site. Write the workplan: the data you need and from whom, the report templates and key tables for each, a timeline working back from the committee meeting date, review and sign-off steps, and how you will explain the numbers to board members without finance backgrounds.

rubric.description: Tasks, owners, data sources and deadlines are specific and work back from the meeting date.
The quarterly report and the special report have different, appropriate structures (variance tables versus a cost model with assumptions).
Includes reconciliation and review steps and a plain-language narrative for non-finance readers.

reference_answer_outline: Data: general ledger close, payroll, program enrollment, grant restrictions; owners in accounting and programs.
Quarterly: budget versus actual by program, variance explanations above a threshold, cash position.
Special: start-up and annual operating costs, staffing ratios, funding sources, break-even enrollment, sensitivity table.
Timeline: close plus five days, draft, director review, CFO sign-off, packet sent one week before meeting.
Narrative: three key messages and a one-page summary chart.

tasks.task_intent: Examine the books and accounting systems to judge whether transactions are recorded efficiently, effectively and according to accepted accounting practice.
tasks.prompt: You are reviewing the accounting system of a 25-employee landscaping company before its first external review engagement. The owner keeps the books in a small-business accounting package, the office manager both writes checks and reconciles the bank account, and revenue is recorded when cash comes in. Create the review checklist and a short findings memo: items covering revenue recognition, accrual versus cash basis, segregation of duties, bank reconciliations, fixed assets and depreciation, payroll, and system access; then summarize the top three issues with recommendations sized for a small company.

rubric.description: Checklist covers recognition policies, reconciliations, cutoff, asset records, payroll and access controls with what evidence to inspect.
Correctly identifies cash-basis revenue as an issue if accrual-basis statements are needed, and the duty overlap as a control weakness.
Recommendations are realistic for a small business, such as owner review of reconciliations and bank statements, instead of hiring more staff.

reference_answer_outline: Revenue: when work is completed versus when paid; unbilled and deferred amounts at year-end.
Reconciliations: monthly, reviewed and signed by the owner; check the most recent three.
Fixed assets: trucks and mowers on a schedule with depreciation method.
Payroll: tax filings timely, seasonal worker classification.
Top issues: cash-basis revenue, duty overlap, no access controls; compensating controls suggested.

tasks.format: customer call script and resolution note
tasks.task_intent: Talk with customers to settle complaints and confirm credit and financial transactions.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a small-business customer of a credit union calls angry that her line-of-credit application was declined and that a payment she made last month is shown as late on her statement. Write the call script you would follow as the credit analyst: how you verify her identity, how you investigate the late-payment record, what you can and cannot explain about the credit decision (including adverse action notice rules), how you de-escalate, and the written resolution note for the file.

rubric.description: Verifies identity before discussing details and traces the payment through records (posting date, method, cutoff time).
Explains the decline using the actual reasons in the adverse action notice, without promising outcomes or sharing other customers' data.
De-escalates professionally, offers concrete next steps (correction if posting error, reapplication guidance) and documents the outcome.

reference_answer_outline: Identity check using the institution's procedure.
Look up the payment: if received before the due-date cutoff, correct the record and the credit-bureau report if it was reported.
Decline reasons from the notice, such as debt-to-income or time in business; how to request the credit report used.
Acknowledge frustration, summarize, agree on a follow-up date.
File note: issue, findings, corrections, commitments, date and analyst name.

tasks.task_intent: Use financial models to solve financial problems or to judge how a transaction would affect finances or capital.
tasks.prompt: A regional coffee-roasting company (invented figures: revenue 12 million, EBITDA 1.8 million, debt 3 million) is deciding whether to buy a competitor for 6 million funded by a new term loan, expecting 400,000 in yearly cost savings after year one. Build a simple model (describe its structure and show key numbers): pro forma revenue and EBITDA, debt and leverage ratios, interest coverage, and a five-year discounted cash flow or payback view of the deal. Write a memo with your conclusion and a sensitivity table for savings and interest rate.

rubric.description: Model has clear inputs, calculations and outputs, with assumptions stated and kept separate.
Leverage, coverage and valuation figures are computed correctly and consistently.
Sensitivity analysis shows how the conclusion changes under plausible downside cases.

reference_answer_outline: Inputs tab: prices, growth, savings ramp, loan rate and term.
Pro forma EBITDA combined plus synergies; leverage equals total debt over EBITDA.
Interest coverage equals EBITDA over interest; compare with lender comfort ranges.
Net present value of incremental cash flows minus price; payback years.
Sensitivity grid of savings achieved versus interest rate; recommendation with conditions.

tasks.task_intent: Write reports that assess how risky it is to extend credit or lend money.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a regional bank is asked for a 2 million working-capital line by an auto-parts distributor whose largest customer accounts for 35 percent of sales, whose inventory has grown faster than sales, and whose current ratio fell from 1.8 to 1.3 in two years. Write the credit risk report: business and industry overview, financial ratio analysis (liquidity, leverage, efficiency), qualitative risks, a risk rating on a stated scale with justification, and the structure and covenants that would make the risk acceptable.

rubric.description: Uses relevant ratios (current ratio, inventory days, debt to equity, coverage) and interprets trends, not just levels.
Recognizes customer concentration and inventory build-up as key risks and assesses their potential impact.
Proposes structure (borrowing base, covenants, reporting) that directly addresses the identified risks.

reference_answer_outline: Overview: products, customers, supplier terms, cyclical auto sector.
Ratios: declining liquidity, rising inventory days, leverage trend.
Concentration risk: impact if the top customer leaves.
Rating with rationale on the bank's scale.
Structure: borrowing base tied to receivables and inventory with advance rates, minimum coverage covenant, monthly aging reports.

tasks.task_intent: Approve loans that fall within one's lending authority and send those above it to management.
tasks.prompt: You are a loan officer with authority to approve consumer auto loans up to 40,000 with debt-to-income up to 43 percent and credit scores of 660 and above. Three invented applications arrive: (A) 28,000, DTI 38 percent, score 702; (B) 45,000, DTI 31 percent, score 760; (C) 22,000, DTI 46 percent, score 690 with a recent job change. Write a decision memo for each: approve, decline, or refer, with reasons tied to policy, any conditions, and how the referral to your manager is documented. Add a note on fair lending consistency.

rubric.description: Approves only within limits, refers B for amount, and handles C's DTI exception properly (refer or decline per policy).
Each decision cites the specific policy criteria and any compensating factors.
Applies criteria consistently regardless of protected characteristics and documents referrals and exceptions.

reference_answer_outline: A: within all limits; approve with standard verification of income and insurance.
B: strong credit but over the 40,000 limit; refer to the manager with a recommendation.
C: DTI above policy; refer as an exception with compensating factors or decline with an adverse action notice.
Referral memo: summary, policy exception, recommendation.
Fair lending: same criteria and documentation for every applicant.

tasks.task_intent: Report orally or in writing on economic trends, particular companies and whole industries.
tasks.prompt: Prepare a 10-minute investment-committee briefing on one publicly traded industry you choose (for example, regional airlines, or solar equipment). Using public sources (annual reports, government statistics, industry data), cover: current industry drivers, two companies compared on growth, margins and leverage, key risks over the next two years, and your view. Deliver it as slide titles with key points plus a one-page written summary, with every figure cited.

rubric.description: Uses cited, current public data and distinguishes facts from forecasts and opinions.
Company comparison uses consistent metrics and explains differences.
Ends with a defensible view, key risks, and what evidence would change the view.

reference_answer_outline: Industry drivers such as fuel costs, demand trends, regulation or interest rates.
Comparison table: revenue growth, operating margin, debt to EBITDA, free cash flow.
Risks: cyclical demand, input costs, policy changes.
View: overweight, neutral or underweight with reasoning.
Sources listed with dates.

tasks.task_intent: Talk with customers to settle complaints and confirm credit and financial transactions.
tasks.prompt: Invented case: a commercial customer of a bank says three wire transfers totaling 18,000 on its statement were never authorized, and also disputes a fee for exceeding its credit-line limit. As the credit analyst on the relationship team, write the procedure you would follow: immediate steps to protect the account, how you verify each transaction (authorization logs, callbacks, IP or device records), how the over-limit fee is reviewed, communication with the customer at each stage, and the final resolution letter.

rubric.description: Secures the account promptly (block, credential reset) and escalates potential fraud to the right team.
Checks authorization evidence for each transfer and reviews the fee against the credit agreement and actual balances.
Gives the customer timelines and a professional, specific resolution letter.

reference_answer_outline: Freeze online wire capability; refer to the fraud team; preserve records.
Pull wire authorization logs, approval user IDs, callback records, device data.
Fee review: compare balances with the line limit and agreement terms; reverse if posted in error.
Update the customer within set timeframes.
Letter stating findings, any credits, and security recommendations such as dual approval.

tasks.task_intent: Meet loan applicants to collect information for their applications and respond to their questions on how lending works.
tasks.prompt: A first-time home buyer couple, both in their twenties with one gig-economy income and one salaried income, books a meeting to apply for a mortgage. Write your interview guide: the information and documents you need (and why for each), how you explain the steps from application to closing, the questions they are likely to ask (down payment, rate locks, credit checks) with plain-language answers, how you handle variable gig income, and the follow-up checklist you hand them.

rubric.description: Lists the documents and data needed and explains why, including how variable income is documented.
Explains the stages and timelines accurately in plain language.
Answers questions without steering or promising approval, and gives a clear follow-up checklist.

reference_answer_outline: Documents: ID, pay stubs, W-2s or tax returns, two years of 1099 and bank statements for gig income, asset statements.
Process: application, disclosures, appraisal, underwriting, conditions, closing.
Explain rate locks, down payment options, and credit inquiry effects.
Gig income: typically averaged over two years; explain why.
Checklist with dates and contact information.

tasks.task_intent: Gather and study data on customers' characteristics, preferences, needs and purchasing patterns to find promising markets and what drives demand.
tasks.prompt: A small company making plant-based protein snacks sells mostly through two grocery chains and wants to know which new customer groups to target next year. Design the research and a mock segmentation: research questions, data sources (store sales data, a customer survey, public census or category reports), the survey sample and key questions, the segmentation variables and method, three resulting segments described with clearly invented figures, and which segment you would prioritize and why.

rubric.description: Questions, sources and sample are appropriate and the survey avoids leading or double-barreled questions.
Segments are based on meaningful variables (needs, usage occasions, price sensitivity, demographics) and are distinct and reachable.
Chooses a segment using explicit criteria (size, growth, fit, competition, profitability) and notes data limits.

reference_answer_outline: Questions: who buys, when and why, what alternatives, price tolerance.
Sources: retailer scan data, loyalty-card summaries if available, a 600-person online panel survey, census demographics.
Method: cluster analysis on needs and behavior variables, profiled by demographics.
Example segments: fitness-focused snackers, busy parents buying for lunchboxes, flexitarian grazers.
Priority segment with sizing logic and next step such as a test campaign.

tasks.format: donor database design and cleanup plan
tasks.task_intent: Set up or refresh the database that tracks donors.
tasks.prompt: An animal shelter tracks 6,000 donors in three spreadsheets (event sign-ups, online gifts, and a volunteer list), with duplicates, missing addresses, and no record of who asked not to be mailed. Write a plan to create a single donor database in a low-cost donor-management tool: the record structure (individuals, households, gifts, communications, preferences), the deduplication and cleanup rules, how consent and do-not-contact preferences are stored, data-entry standards for staff, and three reports the development director will get monthly.

rubric.description: Separates people, households, gifts and interactions, and captures gift type, date, amount, campaign and soft credits.
Has clear matching and merge rules and stores communication preferences and opt-outs so they are honored.
Monthly reports support fundraising decisions (retention, lapsed donors, campaign results).

reference_answer_outline: Entities: constituent, household, gift, pledge, campaign, communication preference.
Matching on name plus email or address; manual review for uncertain matches; merge log.
Opt-out and channel preferences as required fields; suppression lists applied to every mailing.
Entry standards: naming format, address verification, gift acknowledgment within 48 hours.
Reports: donor retention rate, lapsed donors over 12 months, gifts by campaign.

tasks.task_intent: Find, assess or buy the hardware and software needed to run online marketing campaigns.
tasks.prompt: A family-owned outdoor-gear store with an online shop wants to grow search traffic and run its first paid search campaigns with a tool budget of 300 per month. Evaluate the software it needs: list the functions required (keyword research, rank tracking, site audit, analytics, ad management, reporting), compare at least three real tool options or bundles on features, cost, learning curve and data privacy, describe a two-week trial plan, and recommend a stack within budget.

rubric.description: Starts from campaign needs and maps tools to functions rather than listing popular products.
Compares options on consistent criteria with current, verifiable pricing or noted as estimates.
Defines success measures for the trial and recommends a stack that fits budget and staff skills.

reference_answer_outline: Functions mapped to free platform tools (search console, analytics, ad platform) plus one paid SEO suite.
Comparison table with monthly cost, features, user seats, data handling.
Trial: run a site audit, research 50 keywords, set up conversion tracking.
Success: setup time, data accuracy versus platform data, ease of use for the owner.
Recommendation and review after three months.

tasks.task_intent: Write up research findings, showing the data in charts and turning complicated results into clear prose.
tasks.prompt: Invented results: a survey of 800 gym members about a new app feature found 62 percent interested, but only 24 percent willing to pay 5 per month; interest was highest among members under 35 and lowest among those who visit fewer than twice a week; open-ended answers mention privacy worries. Write a two-page findings report for the product team: an executive summary with three key insights, two or three charts you would include (describe them, with correct chart types), the margin of error, what the data do not show, and recommendations.

rubric.description: Leads with decision-relevant insights rather than restating every number.
Chooses suitable charts, reports margin of error correctly for the sample, and avoids overstating subgroup differences.
States limits (stated versus actual willingness to pay, sample bias) and gives actionable recommendations.

reference_answer_outline: Insight: strong interest but low willingness to pay; freemium or bundling may fit better.
Charts: bar chart of interest by age group, stacked bar of willingness to pay by visit frequency.
Margin of error about plus or minus 3.5 points at 95 percent for the full sample; wider for subgroups.
Limits: survey intent overstates purchase; members only, not prospects.
Recommend a pricing test and addressing privacy in the feature design.

tasks.task_intent: Lead or coordinate fundraising that happens on the web, for example web auctions and giving pages.
tasks.prompt: A youth music nonprofit wants to raise 40,000 in a 24-hour online giving day plus a week-long online auction of donated items. Write the campaign plan: goal breakdown and donor targets, platform requirements (donation page, auction tool, payment fees, receipts), the communications calendar across email and social media, how matching gifts and peer-to-peer fundraisers are used, volunteer roles, and how you measure results and thank donors.

rubric.description: Breaks the goal into donor counts and average gifts by source with a plausible conversion assumption.
Covers platform setup, fees, legal or tax receipt requirements and a day-by-day communications calendar.
Includes metrics (donors, new donors, conversion, cost per dollar raised) and a prompt thank-you plan.

reference_answer_outline: Goal split: matching gift pool, board giving, peer fundraisers, general donors, auction proceeds.
Platform: mobile-friendly donation page, auction tool with bidding rules, fee coverage option, automatic receipts.
Calendar: save-the-date, launch, hourly updates on the day, final push, results post.
Volunteers: social media monitors, auction item intake, thank-you callers.
Measure and thank within 48 hours; report impact to donors.

tasks.task_intent: Work with merchants, site owners, bloggers and online editors to earn well-placed links to a site.
tasks.prompt: The outdoor-gear store from your earlier work published a detailed guide to choosing a first backpacking tent. Write a link-outreach plan for it: how you identify relevant sites (trail clubs, hiking blogs, local tourism pages), a short personalized outreach email, what value you offer in return, how you track contacts and results, and the practices you will avoid because they break search-engine guidelines or advertising disclosure rules (such as paying for followed links without disclosure).

rubric.description: Targets sites whose audience genuinely benefits, with criteria for relevance and quality.
Email is personalized, concise and offers real value without manipulation.
Avoids link schemes and undisclosed paid placements and tracks outreach in a simple log with outcomes.

reference_answer_outline: Prospect list from searches for trail guides, club gear lists and local outdoor event pages.
Email: specific reason the guide helps their readers, offer of a quote or local workshop.
Value: expert input, discount for club members disclosed, guest article.
Tracker with site, contact, date, response, link earned.
Avoid buying links, link exchanges at scale, hidden links; paid placements marked as sponsored.
